code: ttt_empty_board <- function() matrix('_', ncol = 3, nrow = 3)  ttt_state2label <- function(state) paste(state, collapse = '')  ttt_label2state <- function(label) matrix(strsplit(label, "")[[1]], nrow = 3, ncol = 3)  ttt_available_actions <- function(state) {   if (length(state) == 1L) state <- ttt_label2state(state)   which(state == "_") }  ttt_result <- function(state, player, action) {   if (length(state) == 1L) state <- ttt_label2state(state)      if (state[action] != "_")     stop("Illegal action.")      state[action] <- player   state } b <- ttt_empty_board() b <- ttt_result(b, 'x', 1) b <- ttt_result(b, 'o', 4) b <- ttt_result(b, 'x', 2) b <- ttt_result(b, 'o', 5) b <- ttt_result(b, 'x', 3) b #>      [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] "x"  "o"  "_"  #> [2,] "x"  "o"  "_"  #> [3,] "x"  "_"  "_"  ttt_state2label(b) #> [1] "xxxoo____"  ttt_available_actions(b) #> [1] 6 7 8 9 ttt_terminal <- function(state) {   if (length(state) == 1L) state <- ttt_label2state(state)      # Check the board for a win and return one of    # 'x', 'o', 'd' (draw), or 'n' (for next move)   win_possibilities <- rbind(state, t(state), diag(state), diag(t(state)))      wins <- apply(win_possibilities, MARGIN = 1, FUN = function(x) {     if (x[1] != '_' && length(unique(x)) == 1) x[1]     else '_'   })      if (any(wins == 'x'))      return('x')      if (any(wins == 'o'))      return('o')      # Check for draw   if (sum(state == '_') < 1) {     return('d')   }      return('n') } b #>      [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] "x"  "o"  "_"  #> [2,] "x"  "o"  "_"  #> [3,] "x"  "_"  "_" ttt_terminal(b) #> [1] "x"

code: start <- ttt_state2label(ttt_empty_board()) start #> [1] "_________"  P <- function(model, action, start.state) {   action <- as.integer(action)      # absorbing states   if (start.state %in% c('win', 'loss', 'draw', 'illegal')) {     return(structure(1, names = start.state))   }      # avoid illegal action by going to the very expensive illegal state   if (!(action %in% ttt_available_actions(start.state))) {     return(structure(1, names = "illegal"))   }      # make x's move   next_state <- ttt_result(start.state, 'x', action)      # terminal?   term <- ttt_terminal(next_state)   if (term == 'x') {     return(structure(1, names = "win"))   } else if (term == 'o') {     return(structure(1, names = "loss"))   } else if (term == 'd') {     return(structure(1, names = "draw"))   }      # it is o's turn, try all available actions   actions_of_o <- ttt_available_actions(next_state)   possible_end_states <- lapply(     actions_of_o,     FUN = function(a)       ttt_result(next_state, 'o', a)   )      # fix terminal states   term <- sapply(possible_end_states, ttt_terminal)   possible_end_states <- sapply(possible_end_states, ttt_state2label)   possible_end_states[term == 'x'] <- 'win'   possible_end_states[term == 'o'] <- 'loss'   possible_end_states[term == 'd'] <- 'draw'      possible_end_states <- unique(possible_end_states)      return(structure(rep(1 / length(possible_end_states),                        length(possible_end_states)),                     names = possible_end_states)) } S <- union(c('win', 'loss', 'draw', 'illegal'),            reachable_states(P, start_state = start, actions = A)) head(S) #> [1] "win"       "loss"      "draw"      "illegal"   "xoxo_ox__" "xoxoo_xxo" length(S) #> [1] 2527

code: library("markovDP") gw_matrix(gw_init(dim = c(3, 4))) #>      [,1]     [,2]     [,3]     [,4]     #> [1,] "s(1,1)" "s(1,2)" "s(1,3)" "s(1,4)" #> [2,] "s(2,1)" "s(2,2)" "s(2,3)" "s(2,4)" #> [3,] "s(3,1)" "s(3,2)" "s(3,3)" "s(3,4)" gw <- gw_init(dim = c(3, 4),         start = "s(3,1)",         goal = "s(1,4)",         absorbing_states = c("s(1,4)", "s(2,4)"),         blocked_states = "s(2,2)",         state_labels = list(             "s(3,1)" = "Start",             "s(2,4)" = "-1",             "s(1,4)" = "Goal: +1") ) gw_matrix(gw) #>      [,1]     [,2]     [,3]     [,4]     #> [1,] "s(1,1)" "s(1,2)" "s(1,3)" "s(1,4)" #> [2,] "s(2,1)" NA       "s(2,3)" "s(2,4)" #> [3,] "s(3,1)" "s(3,2)" "s(3,3)" "s(3,4)" P <- function(model, action, start.state) {   action <- match.arg(action, choices = A(model))      P <- structure(numeric(length(S(model))), names = S(model))      # absorbing states   if (start.state %in% model$info$absorbing_states) {     P[start.state] <- 1     return(P)   }      if (action %in% c("up", "down")) {     error_direction <- c("right", "left")   } else {     error_direction <- c("up", "down")   }      rc <- gw_s2rc(start.state)   delta <- list(     up = c(-1, 0),     down = c(+1, 0),     right = c(0, +1),     left = c(0, -1)   )      # there are 3 directions. For blocked directions, stay in place   # 1) action works .8   rc_new <- gw_rc2s(rc + delta[[action]])   if (rc_new %in% S(model))     P[rc_new] <- .8   else     P[start.state] <- .8      # 2) off to the right .1   rc_new <- gw_rc2s(rc + delta[[error_direction[1]]])   if (rc_new %in% S(model))     P[rc_new] <- .1   else     P[start.state] <-  P[start.state] + .1      # 3) off to the left .1   rc_new <- gw_rc2s(rc + delta[[error_direction[2]]])   if (rc_new %in% S(model))     P[rc_new] <- .1   else     P[start.state] <-  P[start.state] + .1      P   } R <- rbind(   R_(                         value = -0.04),   R_(end.state = "s(2,4)",    value = -1 - 0.04),   R_(end.state = "s(1,4)",    value = +1 - 0.04),   R_(start.state = "s(2,4)",  value = 0),   R_(start.state = "s(1,4)",  value = 0) ) Maze <- MDP(   name = "Stuart Russell's 3x4 Maze",   discount = 1,   horizon = Inf,   states = gw$states,   actions = gw$actions,   start = "s(3,1)",   transition_model = P,   reward = R,   info = gw$info )  Maze #> MDPModel, MDP - Stuart Russell's 3x4 Maze #>   Discount factor: 1 #>   Horizon: Inf epochs #>   Size: 4 actions / 11 states #>   Storage: transition prob as function / reward as data.frame. Total size: 28.5 Kb #>   Start: s(3,1) #>   Model list components: 'name', 'discount', 'horizon', 'states', #>     'actions', 'start', 'transition_model', 'reward', 'info'

title: Infrastructure for Discrete-Time Markov Decision Processes (MDP)
text: Markov decision process (MDP) (Bellman 1957; Howard 1960) discrete-time stochastic control process. time step, agent can perform actions affect system (.e., may cause system state change). agent’s goal maximize expected future rewards depend sequence system state agent’s actions future. Solving MDP means finding optimal (least good) policy guides agent’s actions. markovDP package provides infrastructure work MDPs R. focus convenience formulating MDPs small medium sized state spaces multiple ways, support sparse representations (using sparse matrices, lists data.frames) visualization results. key components implemented C++ speed computation. package provides following popular tabular methods: Value Iteration (Bellman 1957) Modified Policy Iteration (Howard 1960; Puterman Shin 1978) Prioritized Sweeping (Moore Atkeson 1993; Andre et al. 1997; Li Littman 2008) Primal Formulation (Manne 1960) Monte Carlo Control Exploring Starts (Sutton Barto 2018) -policy Monte Carlo Control (Sutton Barto 2018) -policy Monte Carlo Control (Sutton Barto 2018) Random-sample one-step tabular Q-planning (Sutton Barto 2018) Q-Learning (Watkins Dayan 1992) 1-step Sarsa (Rummery Niranjan 1994) Expected Sarsa (Sutton Barto 2018) n-step Sarsa (Sutton Barto 2018) Sarsa(lamba) (Sutton Barto 2018) Watkins’s Q(lamba) (Sutton Barto 2018) 1-step Sarsa (Sutton Barto 2018; Geramifard et al. 2013) Sarsa(lambda) (Sutton Barto 2018) GTD(lambda) (Sutton Barto 2018) implementations follow description (Russell Norvig 2020) (Sutton Barto 2018). implementations represent state space explicitly, problems small medium state spaces can used. title: Bellman Update and Bellman operator — bellman_update
text: Bellman update updates value function given model applying Bellman equation update rule state: $$v_{k+1}(s) \leftarrow \max_{\\mathcal{}(s)} \sum_{s'} p(s' | s,) [r(s,, s') + \gamma v_k(s')]$$ Bellman update moves estimated value function \(V\) closer optimal value function \(v_*\). Bellman operator \(B_\pi\) updates value function given model, policy \(\pi\): $$(B_\pi v)(s) = \sum_{\\mathcal{}} \pi(|s) \sum_{s'} p(s' | s,) [r(s,,s') + \gamma v(s')]$$ Bellman error \(\delta = B_\pi v - v\). Bellman operator reduces Bellman error moves value function closer fixed point true value function: $$v_\pi = B_\pi v_\pi.$$

code: # define an MDP for Tic-Tac-Toe  # state description: matrix with the characters _, x, and o #                    can be converted into a label of 9 characters  # set of actions A <- as.character(1:9)  # helper functions ttt_empty_board <- function() matrix('_', ncol = 3, nrow = 3)  ttt_state2label <- function(state) paste(state, collapse = '')  ttt_label2state <- function(label) matrix(strsplit(label, "")[[1]],                                            nrow = 3, ncol = 3)  ttt_available_actions <- function(state) {   if (length(state) == 1L) state <- ttt_label2state(state)   which(state == "_") }  ttt_result <- function(state, player, action) {   if (length(state) == 1L) state <- ttt_label2state(state)      if (state[action] != "_")     stop("Illegal action.")      state[action] <- player   state }  ttt_terminal <- function(state) {   if (length(state) == 1L) state <- ttt_label2state(state)      # Check the board for a win and return one of    # 'x', 'o', 'd' (draw), or 'n' (for next move)   win_possibilities <- rbind(state,                               t(state),                               diag(state),                               diag(t(state)))    wins <- apply(win_possibilities, MARGIN = 1, FUN = function(x) {     if (x[1] != '_' && length(unique(x)) == 1) x[1]     else '_'   })    if (any(wins == 'x'))      return('x')    if (any(wins == 'o'))      return('o')    # Check for draw   if (sum(state == '_') < 1)     return('d')    return('n') }  # define the transition function:  #     * return a probability vector for an action in a start state #     * we define the special states 'win', 'loss', and 'draw' P <- function(model, action, start.state) {   action <- as.integer(action)      # absorbing states   if (start.state %in% c('win', 'loss', 'draw', 'illegal')) {     return(structure(1, names = start.state))   }      # avoid illegal action by going to the very expensive illegal state   if (!(action %in% ttt_available_actions(start.state))) {     return(structure(1, names = "illegal"))   }      # make x's move   next_state <- ttt_result(start.state, 'x', action)      # terminal?   term <- ttt_terminal(next_state)   if (term == 'x') {     return(structure(1, names = "win"))   } else if (term == 'o') {     return(structure(1, names = "loss"))   } else if (term == 'd') {     return(structure(1, names = "draw"))   }      # it is o's turn   actions_of_o <- ttt_available_actions(next_state)   possible_end_states <- lapply(     actions_of_o,     FUN = function(a)       ttt_result(next_state, 'o', a)   )      # fix terminal states   term <- sapply(possible_end_states, ttt_terminal)   possible_end_states <- sapply(possible_end_states, ttt_state2label)   possible_end_states[term == 'x'] <- 'win'   possible_end_states[term == 'o'] <- 'loss'   possible_end_states[term == 'd'] <- 'draw'      possible_end_states <- unique(possible_end_states)      return(structure(rep(1 / length(possible_end_states),                        length(possible_end_states)),                     names = possible_end_states)) }  # define the reward R <- rbind(   R_(                    value = 0),   R_(end.state = 'win',  value = +1),   R_(end.state = 'loss', value = -1),   R_(end.state = 'draw', value = +.5),   R_(end.state = 'illegal', value = -Inf),   # Note: there is no more reward once the agent is in a terminal state   R_(start.state = 'win',  value = 0),   R_(start.state = 'loss', value = 0),   R_(start.state = 'draw', value = 0),   R_(start.state = 'illegal', value = 0) )  # start state start <- ttt_state2label(ttt_empty_board()) start #> [1] "_________"  # find the reachable state space S <- union(c('win', 'loss', 'draw', 'illegal'),           reachable_states(P, start_state = start, actions = A)) head(S) #> [1] "win"       "loss"      "draw"      "illegal"   "xoxo_ox__" "xoxoo_xxo"  tictactoe <- MDP(S, A, P, R, discount = 1, start = start, name = "TicTacToe") tictactoe #> MDPModel, MDP - TicTacToe #>   Discount factor: 1 #>   Horizon: Inf epochs #>   Size: 9 actions / 2527 states #>   Storage: transition prob as function / reward as data.frame. Total size: 274.6 Kb #>   Start: _________ #>   Model list components: ‘name’, ‘discount’, ‘horizon’, ‘states’, #>     ‘actions’, ‘start’, ‘transition_model’, ‘reward’, ‘info’

title: Linear Function Approximation — linear_function_approximation
text: popular method implemented uses linear preference function $$h(s,,\boldsymbol{w}) = \boldsymbol{w}^\top\phi(s,).$$ action highest preference greedy action. represents stochastic policy, preference scores can converted probabilities using softmax function $$\hat{\pi}(|s,\boldsymbol{w}) = \frac{e^{h(s,,\boldsymbol{w})}}{\sum_b e^{h(s,b,\boldsymbol{w})}}$$ gradient $$\nabla \hat{\pi}(|s,\boldsymbol{w}) = \hat{\pi}(|s,\boldsymbol{w}) [\phi(s,) - \sum_b \hat{\pi}(b|s,\boldsymbol{w}) \phi(s,b)].$$ last term represents feature vector reduced expected feature vector across actions current policy. pushes approximation make chosen action \(\) likely. use gradient log-policy avoids multiplying \(\hat{\pi}(|s,\boldsymbol{w})\) numerically stable: $$\nabla log\ \hat{\pi}(|s,\boldsymbol{w}) = \phi(s,)-\sum_b \hat{\pi}(b|s,\boldsymbol{w})  \phi(s,b).$$ gradient log-policy points direction original gradient.

this model has no state specified line_maze #> MDPSample, MDP - line maze [-10,+10] #>   Discount factor: 0.9 #>   Horizon: Inf epochs #>   Size: 2 actions / undefined state space #>   Start: s(0) #>   List components: ‘name’, ‘discount’, ‘horizon’, ‘actions’, ‘states’, #>     ‘start’, ‘absorbing_states’, ‘transition_model’, ‘info’ S(line_maze) #> NULL  # set the states in the model line_maze$states <- states line_maze #> MDPSample, MDP - line maze [-10,+10] #>   Discount factor: 0.9 #>   Horizon: Inf epochs #>   Size: 2 actions / 21 states #>   Start: s(0) #>   List components: ‘name’, ‘discount’, ‘horizon’, ‘actions’, ‘states’, #>     ‘start’, ‘absorbing_states’, ‘transition_model’, ‘info’  sol <- solve_MDP(line_maze, method = "TD:q_learning",    horizon = 100, n = 100, epsilon = .8)  policy(sol) #>     state         V action #> 1   s(-1) 2.5001888   left #> 2  s(-10) 0.0000000  right #> 3   s(-2) 3.2589494   left #> 4   s(-3) 4.1230376   left #> 5   s(-4) 5.0752757   left #> 6   s(-5) 6.0703161   left #> 7   s(-6) 7.0287817   left #> 8   s(-7) 7.9976524   left #> 9   s(-8) 8.9895388   left #> 10  s(-9) 9.9990328   left #> 11   s(0) 1.7037361   left #> 12   s(1) 1.3041920   left #> 13  s(10) 0.0000000  right #> 14   s(2) 1.0743627   left #> 15   s(3) 0.8032204   left #> 16   s(4) 0.3581580   left #> 17   s(5) 0.1192231   left #> 18   s(6) 0.1333712  right #> 19   s(7) 0.5072045  right #> 20   s(8) 1.8258678  right #> 21   s(9) 5.7824847  right plot_value_function(sol)   # Example 2: Find the states to define an MDP for Tic-Tac-Toe  # state description: matrix with the characters _, x, and o #                    can be converted into a label of 9 characters  # set of actions A <- as.character(1:9)  # helper functions ttt_empty_board <- function() matrix('_', ncol = 3, nrow = 3)  ttt_state2label <- function(state) paste(state, collapse = '')  ttt_label2state <- function(label) matrix(strsplit(label, "")[[1]],                                            nrow = 3, ncol = 3)  ttt_available_actions <- function(state) {   if (length(state) == 1L) state <- ttt_label2state(state)   which(state == "_") }  ttt_result <- function(state, player, action) {   if (length(state) == 1L) state <- ttt_label2state(state)      if (state[action] != "_")     stop("Illegal action.")      state[action] <- player   state }  ttt_terminal <- function(state) {   if (length(state) == 1L) state <- ttt_label2state(state)      # Check the board for a win and return one of    # 'x', 'o', 'd' (draw), or 'n' (for next move)   win_possibilities <- rbind(state,                               t(state),                               diag(state),                               diag(t(state)))    wins <- apply(win_possibilities, MARGIN = 1, FUN = function(x) {     if (x[1] != '_' && length(unique(x)) == 1) x[1]     else '_'   })    if (any(wins == 'x'))      return('x')    if (any(wins == 'o'))      return('o')    # Check for draw   if (sum(state == '_') < 1)     return('d')    return('n') }  # define the transition function:  #     * return a probability vector for an action in a start state #     * we define the special states 'win', 'loss', and 'draw' P <- function(model, action, start.state) {   action <- as.integer(action)      # absorbing states   if (start.state %in% c('win', 'loss', 'draw', 'illegal')) {     return(structure(1, names = start.state))   }      # avoid illegal action by going to the very expensive illegal state   if (!(action %in% ttt_available_actions(start.state))) {     return(structure(1, names = "illegal"))   }      # make x's move   next_state <- ttt_result(start.state, 'x', action)      # terminal?   term <- ttt_terminal(next_state)   if (term == 'x') {     return(structure(1, names = "win"))   } else if (term == 'o') {     return(structure(1, names = "loss"))   } else if (term == 'd') {     return(structure(1, names = "draw"))   }      # it is o's turn   actions_of_o <- ttt_available_actions(next_state)   possible_end_states <- lapply(     actions_of_o,     FUN = function(a)       ttt_result(next_state, 'o', a)   )      # fix terminal states   term <- sapply(possible_end_states, ttt_terminal)   possible_end_states <- sapply(possible_end_states, ttt_state2label)   possible_end_states[term == 'x'] <- 'win'   possible_end_states[term == 'o'] <- 'loss'   possible_end_states[term == 'd'] <- 'draw'      possible_end_states <- unique(possible_end_states)      return(structure(rep(1 / length(possible_end_states),                        length(possible_end_states)),                     names = possible_end_states)) }  # define the reward R <- rbind(   R_(                    value = 0),   R_(end.state = 'win',  value = +1),   R_(end.state = 'loss', value = -1),   R_(end.state = 'draw', value = +.5),   R_(end.state = 'illegal', value = -Inf),   # Note: there is no more reward once the agent is in a terminal state   R_(start.state = 'win',  value = 0),   R_(start.state = 'loss', value = 0),   R_(start.state = 'draw', value = 0),   R_(start.state = 'illegal', value = 0) )  # start state start <- ttt_state2label(ttt_empty_board()) start #> [1] "_________"  # find the reachable state space S <- union(c('win', 'loss', 'draw', 'illegal'),           reachable_states(P, start_state = start, actions = A)) head(S) #> [1] "win"       "loss"      "draw"      "illegal"   "xoxo_ox__" "xoxoo_xxo"  tictactoe <- MDP(S, A, P, R, discount = 1, start = start, name = "TicTacToe") tictactoe #> MDPModel, MDP - TicTacToe #>   Discount factor: 1 #>   Horizon: Inf epochs #>   Size: 9 actions / 2527 states #>   Storage: transition prob as function / reward as data.frame. Total size: 201.3 Kb #>   Start: _________ #>   Model list components: ‘name’, ‘discount’, ‘horizon’, ‘states’, #>     ‘actions’, ‘start’, ‘transition_model’, ‘reward’, ‘info’  # this MDP takes about 30 seconds to solve using value iteration # sol <- solve_MDP(tictactoe) # policy(sol)[1:10, ]

title: Solve MDPs using Dynamic Programming — solve_MDP_DP
text: following dynamic programming methods implemented using algorithms presented Russell Norvig (2010). (Modified) Policy Iteration (Howard 1960; Puterman Shin 1978) starts random policy iteratively performs sequence (Approximate) policy evaluation estimate value function current policy. Iterative policy evaluation can approximated stopping early k_backups iterations (see policy_evaluation(). case algorithm called modified policy iteration. Policy improvement performed updating policy greedy (see greedy_policy()) respect new value function. algorithm stops converges stable policy (.e., changes two iterations). Note policy typically stabilizes value function converges. Value Iteration (Bellman 1957) starts arbitrary value function (default 0s) iteratively updates value function state using Bellman update equation (see bellman_update()). $$v(s) \leftarrow \max_{\\mathcal{}(s)} \sum_{s'} p(s' | s,) [r(s,, s') + \gamma v(s')]$$ iteration terminated solution converges maximum n iterations reached. Approximate convergence achieved discounted problems (\(\gamma < 1\)) maximal value function change state \(\delta\) $$\delta \le \frac{error (1-\gamma)}{\gamma}.$$ can shown means state value \(error\) value optimal value function. undiscounted problems, use \(\delta \le error\). greedy policy extracted final value function. Value iteration can seen policy iteration policy evaluation truncated one step. Prioritized Sweeping (Moore Atkeson, 1993; Andre et al., 1997; Li Littman, 2008) approximate optimal value function iteratively adjusting one state time. value policy iteration sweep every iteration states, prioritized sweeping updates states order given priority. priority reflects much state value may change given recently updated states can directly reached via action. update order often lead faster convergence compared sweeping whole state space regular value iteration. implement two priority update strategies described PS GenPS Li Littman (2008). PS (Moore Atkeson, 1993) updates priority state \(H(s)\) using: $$        \forall{s \\mathcal{S}}: H_{t+1}(s)  \leftarrow \begin{cases}          \max(H_{t}(s), \Delta_t \max_{\\mathcal{}}(p(s_t|s,)) \text{ } s \ne s_{t+1} \\          \Delta_t \max_{\}(p(s_t|s,) \text{ } s = s_{t+1}          \end{cases}      $$ \(\Delta_t = |V_{t+1}(s_t) - V_t(s_t)| = |E(s_t; V_{t+1})|\), .e., Bellman error updated state. GenPS (Andre et al., 1997) updates state priorities using current Bellman error: $$\forall{s \\mathcal{S}}: H_{t+1}(s) \leftarrow |E(s; V_{t+1})|$$ \(E(s; V_{t+1}) = \max_{\} \left[R(s,) + \gamma \sum_{s \S} p(s'|s,) V(s')\right] - V(s)\) state's Bellman error. update method can chosen using additional parameter H_update character string "PS_random", "PS_error" "GenPS". default H_update = "GenPS". PS, random means priority vector initialized random values (larger 0), error means initialized Bellman error GenPS. However, requires one complete sweep states. implementation stops updating largest priority values states less specified error. Since algorithm sweep whole state space iteration, n converted equivalent number state updates \(n = n\ |S|\).

title: Solve MDPs using Tabular Temporal Differencing — solve_MDP_TD
text: Eligibility traces also look ahead update performed backward looking manner using memory parameter called trace remember states Q-values lead current event. focus tabular Sarsa(\(\lambda\)) forward-view perspective, \(\lambda\)-reward can seen average infinite n-step backups: $$G_t^\lambda = (1-\lambda) \sum_{n=1}^\infty \lambda^{n-1} R_t^{(n)},$$ \(\lambda\) eligibility trace decay factor. implementation uses backward view TD-error $$\delta_t = R_{t+1} + \gamma Q(S_{t+1}, A_{t+1}) - Q(S_{t}, A_{t})$$ update $$Q(s,) = Q(s,) + \alpha \delta_t z_t(s,) \qquad \forall s, .$$ trace updated time step $$z_t(s,) = \gamma z_{t-1}(s,) \qquad \forall s, $$ \(z_t(S_t,A_t) = z_t(S_t,A_t) + 1\). means, trace set one current state action decays parameter \(\lambda\). title: Transformation Functions for Linear Function Approximation — transformation
text: state feature function \(\phi()\) uses raw state feature vectors \(\mathbf{x} = (x_1,x_2, ..., x_m)\) either user-specified constructed parsing state labels form s(feature list) applies transformation functions called basis functions. Implemented basis functions : Linear: additional transformation applied giving \(\phi_0(s) = 1\) intercept \(\phi_i(s) = x_i\) \(= \{1, 2, ..., m\}\). Polynomial basis: $$\phi_i(s) = \prod_{j=1}^m x_j^{c_{,j}},$$ \(c_{1,j}\) integer 0 \(n\) order \(n\) polynomial basis. Radial Basis: RBF. Fourier basis: $$\phi_i(s) = \text{cos}(\pi\mathbf{c}^\cdot \mathbf{x}),$$ \(\mathbf{c}^= [c_1, c_2, ..., c_m]\) \(c_j = [0, ..., n]\), \(n\) order basis. components feature vector \(x\) assumed scaled interval \([0,1]\). fourier basis transformation implemented transformation_fourier_basis(). min max minimums maximums feature vector component used resale \([0,1]\) using \(\frac{x_i - min_i}{max_i - min_i}\) Details transformation described Konidaris et al (2011).
